Color grading has a small working vocabulary. Here is the ladder from the words you have to the words a colorist acts on.

## Core terms

| Term | Plain meaning | Vague word it replaces |
|---|---|---|
| White balance (color temperature) | How orange or blue neutral whites look | "warmer" → "shift white balance toward amber in the skin tones" |
| Contrast | The gap between the darkest and brightest parts | "punchier" → "crush the blacks slightly, keep the highlights" |
| Saturation | How intense the colors are | "cinematic" → "lower saturation in the greens, keep skin natural" |

## What good looks like

Colorists judge skin tones, continuity from shot to shot, and whether the look serves the scene.

Bad brief: "make it more cinematic". Good brief: "teal shadows, warm skin, contrast like the reference frame".

## How to ask for what you want

Template: "For scene ___, the mood is ___. Keep skin ___. Shadows ___, highlights ___. Reference: ___."
